clue.text: Field covered with variety of shady shrubs

indicators.note: something covered by a layer sits wrapped inside it, so the field goes in the middle
a variety is a different version, so the letters that follow come in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a range is an area of open land, as for grazing or shooting

explanation.surface: A garden bed or meadow planted with a mix of shrubs that cast shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the inner piece; the anagram of shady wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are flowering garden bushes with big round heads of blooms, so they are examples of shrubs.

clue.text: Large room, outstanding, sanctified

parts.note: a hall is a big room for gatherings
a debt still outstanding is owed

explanation.surface: A grand chamber, excellent and consecrated, like a cathedral nave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as praise, but here it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or treated as sacred, the same as consecrated by blessing.

clue.text: Follow mother's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is a familiar word for mother; the 's just joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: Advice to obey what your mother taught you.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a doctrine or set of principles laid down by an authority, a body of instruction.

clue.text: Dodgy gear I continue selling

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters that follow are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A market trader admitting they keep flogging suspect goods.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'Dodgy gear' is the stolen goods being sold; 'Dodgy' is really the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctioneering is the business of selling items to the highest bidder, so it is a form of selling.

clue.text: Giant success? End up with hotel

parts.note: to make a go of something is to succeed at it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Asking whether ending up at a hotel counts as a big achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'success' is a loose fit for GO, as in making a go of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant slain by David, and his name is used for any huge person or thing.

clue.text: One in drama at sea left naval officer

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
something at sea is adrift and confused, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone in a seafaring drama has abandoned the navy officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a naval scene perfectly but is the scrambling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking commander of a fleet, a senior commissioned rank in the navy.

clue.text: Inspire scorn, dropping name

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to spurn is to reject with contempt
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Advice to motivate people by being disdainful, but without naming names.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or encourage them, which is to rouse them to act.

clue.text: Picture in doorway catching shaft of light

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a portal is an imposing doorway or gate
a ray is a narrow beam of light

explanation.surface: A painting of a doorway lit by a beam of sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction of someone or something, as a painting or picture is.

clue.text: Rest with engineers present

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to pose a question is to present it

explanation.surface: Taking a break with the engineering team on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like an adjective meaning 'here', but it is the verb, as in presenting a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose means relaxation or sleep, a state of being at ease without exertion.

clue.text: Pass westward around good island, showing sense

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
in an across entry, going west means reading from right to left

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
G is the abbreviation for good
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing a mountain pass heading west round a pleasant island, acting sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: COL, a mountain pass, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, as in 'there is no sense in that', so it means good sense.

clue.text: Sweet advance, seizing moment with run before work

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so one word is clutched inside another

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an op is a work, short for opus

explanation.surface: A boss making a quick advance before a job, as if borrowing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts R ahead of OP. 'Half a mo' is British for 'just a moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a boiled lemon-flavoured candy, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Discount large scam, coming up with goals and beginning to bear burden

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a con is a swindle
L is the abbreviation for large
aims are objectives

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of bear
an onus is a responsibility or burden

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off a big con while pursuing goals and starting to shoulder a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: A no-claims bonus is the British name for a reduced insurance premium earned by not claiming, called a no-claims discount in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonus is a reduction in a car insurance premium for a policyholder who makes no claims, so it is a discount.

clue.text: Instrument in old saloon perhaps popular with audience initially

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a saloon is a type of car, a sedan in American English
something popular is in

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of audience

explanation.surface: A tune played in an old Western saloon bar, a hit with the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Wild West bar, but saloon is the British word for a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, played by blowing.

clue.text: Archives in care of king seized by revolutionaries

indicators.note: something seized by others is held in their grip, so it goes inside

parts.note: reds are communists or revolutionaries
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The royal archives, in the king's keeping, captured by rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Records are documents kept as evidence, and archives are collections of such historical documents.

clue.text: Mountaineer near muddy ground around tor?

indicators.note: going around something wraps it inside
ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: A climber standing near soggy ground at the foot of a rocky outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the earth underfoot but means milled. The question mark warns that a tor is only one kind of hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edmund Hillary, the New Zealander, made the first confirmed ascent of Everest with Tenzing Norgay in 1953.

clue.text: Commercial, in distortion of moral appeal, lacking skill

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
a distortion twists a thing out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a commercial on TV or radio
it means sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A clumsy advert that twists a moral message to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is old slang, still in 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit comes from French for badly handed: clumsy, awkward and inept in movement or tact.

clue.text: Most acute pressure in parts over time

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: shares are portions or parts
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The most intense stress is felt in certain parts over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue just puts the pieces above the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpest and most acute both describe the keenest angle, pain, or mind, the highest degree of keenness.

clue.text: Story by bishop, weak, involving hesitation before church wine

indicators.note: involving something means taking it in, so that piece goes inside

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
frail means feeble or weak
um is a sound of hesitation
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A feeble tale told by a dithering bishop before the church communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Liebfraumilch is a sweetish German white wine from the Rhine region, popular in Britain in the 1970s and 80s.

clue.text: Raised in Nazareth, gifted one with unyielding determination

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted up, read from bottom to top
the answer is contained within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A gifted person brought up in Nazareth who never gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised in Nazareth' evokes Jesus's upbringing; 'Raised' is the signal to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is figuratively someone who keeps battling against the odds and refuses to give in.

clue.text: Lack of restraint in scrap

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to give up or discard a plan

explanation.surface: Losing control during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a brawl, matching the loss of restraint, but it is the verb meaning to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for wild uninhibited freedom and a verb for giving up or discarding something entirely.

clue.text: Protest? It's a thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to raise an objection, verb
second meaning: a material item, noun

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a demonstration is a genuine fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a thing' sounds like modern slang for a trend, but it simply joins two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable the word is a verb meaning to oppose; stressed on the first it is a noun for an item.

clue.text: Potential row after daughter admitted to obsession

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it

parts.note: a bug is a craze, as in 'the travel bug'

indicators.note: after sends the word before it second, behind the daughter that follows

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: A possible family quarrel once the daughter confessed to her fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' here: noise, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Budding as an adjective means developing or promising, as in a budding actor, someone with potential.

clue.text: Judge in revolutionary period accepting part with resistance

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a piece goes inside
a revolution turns things right round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a bit is a part or piece
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A judge during a time of revolution, taking a role in the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person appointed to settle a dispute, so like a judge they decide between parties.

clue.text: Bone from bird endlessly conserved by volunteers

indicators.note: something conserved by others is kept safe within them

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: Volunteer conservationists preserving the skeleton of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a crossword staple for volunteers, from the Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones in the lower leg.

clue.text: Extended barrier in eastern capital? Not on

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
not on says that pair of letters must be taken out

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
London is a capital city, hence the question mark for definition by example
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A long wall stretched across an eastern capital, met with disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' sounds like the British phrase for unacceptable; here it removes the letters ON from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongated means made longer, lengthened or stretched out, just as something extended is.

clue.text: Grand number followed by odd pieces from ballet

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: the odd pieces are the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: letters one, three and five of ballet

explanation.surface: A spectacular dance number followed by fragments of a ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble and grand both mean impressive and stately in appearance, magnificent in scale or bearing.

clue.text: Carry toddler with energy

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pick up the small child energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to haul or lug something around, an informal verb for bearing a load.

clue.text: Engine component about level with small handle

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
a rank is a level in a hierarchy
S is the abbreviation for small
a haft is the handle of a knife, axe or tool

explanation.surface: A mechanic's part described as roughly flush with a short handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crankshaft is the rotating shaft in an engine that turns pistons' up-and-down motion into rotation.
